findings.english_quote: Some suffer from every kind of[k] trouble.
findings.issue: The general word “trouble” loses the specific disorder, instability, or turmoil named by ἀκαταστασίᾳ. This is a distinct item in the list of punishments, not merely a general description encompassing the other afflictions. The lexical rationale acknowledges instability, but the reader text does not convey it.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “Some suffer from every kind of[k] turmoil.” Retain the disclosure that the wording corresponding to πάσῃ is editorially bracketed in the working source. Review the replacement afresh before adoption.

findings.source_quote: ἀλλ᾽ αἰτιῶνται τὸν Κύριον. 6. ὅταν οὖν θλιβῶσι πάσῃ θλίψει, τότε ἐμοὶ παραδίδονται εἰς ἀγαθὴν παιδείαν
findings.english_quote:
It does not occur to them[e] that they have done evil; instead, they blame the Lord.”

“When, then, they suffer every kind of affliction, they are handed over to me for good correction and training.
findings.issue: The closing quotation mark after “Lord” ends the shepherd’s speech, and the following paragraph opens an unattributed new speech containing “me.” The source continues the shepherd’s explanation without a speaker change. This punctuation creates avoidable uncertainty about whose disciplinary authority “me” identifies.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the closing quotation mark after “Lord” so that the next paragraph continues the shepherd’s existing multi-paragraph speech. Review the resulting quotation structure afresh.

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against the complete supplied Greek working text. The standard edition has no concrete fidelity defect identified. The simplified edition needs correction to preserve the specific disorder terminology and uninterrupted speaker attribution. Both retain contextual repentance, reader-facing service language, the unrestricted requests and prosperity assertions, and the final comprehensive negation. The bracketed readings and faith alternative are disclosed without claiming fresh manuscript verification. Acceptance here concerns the supplied working source and disclosures, not authentication of unseen editions, manuscripts, or exhaustive collation.
